summary.text: Crystal structure is the ordered arrangement of atoms, ions or molecules in a crystalline material.
The pattern repeats in all three directions of space, and the smallest repeating group of particles, the unit cell, reflects the symmetry of the whole crystal.
Structure and symmetry play a critical role in physical properties such as cleavage, electronic band structure and optical transparency.

facts.label: Unit cell
facts.value: The smallest repeating unit with the full symmetry of the structure

facts.label: Lattice parameters
facts.value: Three edge lengths and three angles describe a unit cell

facts.label: Space groups
facts.value: 230 describe every symmetric arrangement of particles in 3D space

items.prompt: A crystal may hold billions of atoms. How can a scientist describe all of it by looking at one small group of particles?

options.label: The group is an average of every particle, so the crystal needs no pattern
The whole crystal is built by repeating that group, which carries the crystal's symmetry
The group is the only part that matters, and the rest is filler
The crystal's atoms keep changing places, so only the group stays put

items.explain: The unit cell completely reflects the symmetry and structure of the entire crystal, which is built by repeating it along its principal axes.

items.prompt: A mineral tends to split cleanly along certain flat directions. Which feature of its structure is behind that?

options.label: Planes where its particles are packed more densely
Planes where its particles are far apart
Planes that hold the crystal's coloured impurities
Planes along which the crystal is always perfectly square

items.explain: Cleavage typically occurs preferentially parallel to higher density planes.

items.prompt: A scientist wants to describe the shape of one unit cell in a crystal. How many measurements does she need?

options.label: Two: one length and one angle
Three: the lengths of the three edges only
Six: three edge lengths and three angles
Nine: one for each particle in the cell

items.explain: The unit cell is a parallelepiped described by six lattice parameters: the edge lengths (a, b, c) and the angles between them.

items.prompt: A crystallographer rotates a lattice in a particular way, and it looks the same as before. What is this showing?

options.label: That the lattice has no ordered structure
That the lattice is a liquid in disguise
That the lattice is polluted with impurities
The inherent symmetry that defines a crystal

items.explain: The defining property of a crystal is its inherent symmetry: certain symmetry operations leave the lattice unchanged.

items.prompt: A metal crystal bends and keeps its new shape. Along which direction do its particles shift most easily?

options.label: A sparse direction, which has the most room
A dense direction, which needs less distortion of the lattice
A random direction, since every direction needs the same effort
Directions outside the crystal's symmetry

items.explain: Dislocation glide occurs preferentially along dense directions, because shifting a node in a denser direction requires a lesser distortion of the lattice.

items.prompt: Two faces of the same crystal react with a gas at different rates. What about the faces could explain this?

options.label: They have different densities of surface particles
They are different colours
One is deeper inside the crystal
They contain different numbers of unit cells

items.explain: Reactions occur at or near surface atoms or molecules, so they are sensitive to the density of nodes.
